newsitem.title: UK: Clarke speech to contain no budget hints - sources.
newsitem.headline: Clarke speech to contain no budget hints - sources.

text.p: A speech by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke to the annual conference of the Conservative party on Thursday will contain no hints on the contents of the November budget, political sources said.
Aides to Clarke were last year concerned when the media reported a quip by the Chancellor about taxes as an indication that he intended to cut tax rates in that year's budget.
The sources said in this year's speech "no one will be able to read anything in".
He also said that Clarke would fully back cabinet policy on Europe and there would be no gloss or spin that could be put on his comments.
Clarke is the most pro-European member of the cabinet and he has been forceful in his support for a single European currency.
